entered_claims.text: A method of configuring a camera to view a sequence of positions comprising the steps of: displaying a graphical user interface; displaying a plurality of thumbnails on the graphical user interface with the plurality of thumbnails having associated respective positions of the camera and the respective thumbnails in the plurality of thumbnails providing the field of view of the camera in the respective positions; providing a workspace on the graphical user interface; enabling a user to drag and drop thumbnails to the workspace; and creating a tour for the camera based on the thumbnails in the workspace.
A method as recited in claim 1 wherein the creating step creates a tour for the camera based on the thumbnails in the workspace and the order of the thumbnails.
A method as recited in claim 2 further comprising the step of enabling a user to drag and drop the thumbnails in the workspace to change the order of the presets in the tour for the camera.

A method as recited in claim 2 further comprising the steps of receiving input from a user to delete a selected thumbnail in the workspace and deleting the selected thumbnail in the workspace thereby deleting the preset from the tour.
A method as recited in claim 2 further comprising the step of saving the tour based on user input.

A method as recited in claim 5 further comprising the steps of receiving user input to open a tour that has been saved and opening a tour based on the received user input by displaying thumbnails of the presets in the tour in the workspace.

A method as recited in 6 further comprising the steps of changing the tour that has been opened based on the received user input by enabling a user to modify the preset order of the tour by dragging and dropping the thumbnails displayed in the workspace.

A method as recited in claim 6 further comprising the step of adding a preset to the tour that has been opened based on the received user input by enabling a user to drag and drop a thumbnail displayed on the graphical user interface in the workspace.

A method as recited in claim 6 further comprising the step of removing a preset from a tour that has been opened based on the received user input by receiving user input indicating which thumbnail in the workspace has been selected by the user.

A system for configuring a camera to view a sequence of positions comprising: a processor, a display connected to the processor, an input/output device adapted to communicate with a camera, and a user input device, the processor being adapted to generate a signal to display a graphical user interface on the display with a plurality of thumbnails associated with a camera in communication with the input/output device, the thumbnails having associated respective positions of the camera and the thumbnails providing the field of view of the camera in the respective positions, the processor being further adapted to provide a workspace on the graphical user interface and to enable a user to use the user input device to drag and drop thumbnails in the workspace thereby creating a tour for the camera based on the thumbnails in the workspace.
A system as recited in claim 10 wherein the processor is adapted to create a tour for the camera based on the order of the thumbnails in the workspace.

A system as recited in claim 11 wherein the processor enables a user to use the user input device to drag and drop the thumbnails in the workspace thereby changing the order of the presets in the tour for the camera.
A system as recited in claim 11 wherein the processor is adapted to delete a preset from the tour in response to a preset being selected by a user and an indication that the preset should be deleted.
A system as recited in claim 11 wherein the processor is adapted to open a tour and enable a user to modify the tour by using the user input device.

A non-transitory computer readable medium comprising instructions configured to cause a processor to: display a graphical user interface; display a plurality of thumbnails on the graphical user interface with the plurality of thumbnails having associated respective positions of the camera and the respective thumbnails in the plurality of thumbnails providing the field of view of the camera in the respective positions; provide a workspace on the graphical user interface; enable a user to drag and drop thumbnails to the workspace; and create a tour for the camera based on the thumbnails in the workspace.

A non-transitory computer readable medium as recited in claim 16 wherein the instructions to create a tour for the camera based on the thumbnails in the workspace comprise instructions configured to cause the processor to create a tour for the camera based on the thumbnails in the workspace and the order of the thumbnails.

A non-transitory computer readable medium as recited in claim 16 further comprising instructions configured to cause the processor to enable a user to drag and drop the thumbnails in the workspace to change the order of the presets in the tour for the camera.

A non-transitory computer readable medium as recited in claim 16 further comprising instructions configured to cause the processor to receive input from a user to delete a selected thumbnail in the workspace and to delete the selected thumbnail in the workspace thereby deleting the preset from the tour.

A non-transitory computer readable medium as recited in claim 16 further comprising instructions configured to cause the processor to receive user input to open a tour and to open a tour based on the received user input by displaying thumbnails of the presets in the tour in the workspace.

A non-transitory computer readable medium as recited in claim 20 further comprising instructions configured to cause the processor to enable a user to modify a tour that has been opened by interacting with the thumbnails in the workspace.

A method of controlling a flight obstacle lighting arrangement of a wind power installation, the method comprising:
receiving a first predetermined signal that includes at least one of an item of height information and an item of location information; and
using a switching device coupled to the flight obstacle lighting arrangement to switch off the flight obstacle lighting arrangement upon reception of the first predetermined signal by a receiver coupled to the switching device.

The method according to claim 1, further comprising:
switching on the flight obstacle lighting arrangement upon receipt of when at least one of the following occurs:
a fault;
an absence of the first predetermined signal is not received; and
an incorrect evaluation of the first predetermined signal.
The method according to claim 1, further comprising switching on the flight obstacle lighting arrangement upon receipt of a second predetermined signal.

The method according to claim 3, wherein a central control station transmits at least one of the first predetermined signal and the second predetermined signal through at least one intermediate station to a plurality of transmitting stations.

The method according to claim 4 wherein the plurality of transmitting stations includes either all existing transmitting stations, or transmitting stations selected in accordance with at least one predetermined criteria criterion.

The method according to claim 4 wherein a fault in the first predetermined signal or the second predetermined signal of the central control station causes the at least one intermediate station to transmit a signal to at least a portion of the plurality of transmitting stations, causing the transmitting stations to either switch off, or emit the second predetermined signal.

The method according to claim 4 wherein, in the event of a fault in the signal of an intermediate station, the transmitting stations associated with said intermediate station emit the second predetermined signal.

A system wind power installation comprising:
a flight obstacle lighting arrangement;
a receiver configured to receive a first signal that includes at least one of an item of height information and an item of location information; and
a switching device coupled to the receiver and to the flight obstacle lighting arrangement: the receiver structured to receive a first signal, the switching device stn-etured configured to switch off the flight obstacle lighting arrangement in response to reception of the first signal by the receiver receiving the first signal.

The system wind power installation according to claim 8 wherein, the switching device is structured to switch on the flight obstacle lighting arrangement in response to detection of a fault in the first signal.

The systern wind power installation according to claim 8 wherein upon reception of a second predetermined signal by the receivers the switching device is structured to switch on the flight obstacle lighting arrangement in rcspoinsc to rcocption by the receiver of a second signal.
The systern wind power installation according to claim 8 wherein the flight obstacle lighting arrangement comprises a wind power installation.

A flight obstacle lighting arrangement system of a wind power installation, comprising:
a central control station having a plurality of intermediate stations; and
a plurality of transmitting devices, wherein the plurality of transmitting devices are connected to the central control station by at least one intermediate station and wherein the central control station is structured to emit a control station signal receivable by the at least one intermediate station and wherein the at least one intermediate station is structured to emit a first predetermined signal when the control station signal is present, wherein the first predetermined signal comprises at least one of an item of height information and an item of location information.

The system wind power installation according to claim 8, further comprising at least one entrance door operatively connected to a switch that the switching device, wherein the switching device is structured to activate the flight obstacle lighting arrangement when the at least one entrance door is opened.

The method according to claim 1, wherein the first predetermined signal includes the item of height information, the method further comprising comparing the height information to a threshold value, and
when the height information is less than the threshold value, switching on the flight obstacle lighting arrangement.

The wind power installation according to claim 8, wherein the first signal includes the height information, wherein the switching device is an evaluation and switching device configured to compare the height information to a threshold value, and when the height information is less than the threshold value, using the evaluation and switching device to switch on the flight obstacle lighting arrangement.

A method for producing a silicon carbide ceramic according to Claim 1, wherein: the plural kinds of silicon carbide ceramic powders are composed of high 4H-SiC silicon carbide ceramic powders being silicon carbide ceramic powders having a smaller content ratio of 4H-SiC silicon carbide crystal compared with the content ratio of 4H-SiC silicon carbide crystals in silicon carbide crystals in a silicon carbide ceramic to be produced and high 4H-SiC silicon carbide ceramic powders being silicon carbide ceramic powders having a larger content ratio of 4H-SiC silicon carbide crystal content compared with the content ratio of 4H-SiC silicon carbide crystals in the silicon carbide crystals in the silicon carbide ceramic to be produced; wherein the content ratio of the 4H-SiC silicon carbide crystals in the silicon carbide crystals in the low 4H-SiC silicon carbide ceramic powders is 0.01 to 15 mass%; and the content ratio of the 4H-SiC silicon carbide crystals in the silicon carbide crystals in the high 4H-SiC silicon carbide ceramic powders is 0.5 to 40 mass%.

A method for producing a silicon carbide ceramic according to Claim 2, wherein a difference between the content ratio of the 4H-SiC silicon carbide crystals in the silicon carbide crystals in the low 4H-SiC silicon carbide ceramic powders and the content ratio of the 4H-SiC silicon carbide crystals in the silicon carbide crystals in the high 4H-SiC silicon carbide ceramic powders is 5 to 30 mass%.

A method for producing a silicon carbide ceramic according to any one of Claims 1 to 3, wherein the silicon carbide ceramic to be produced contains 0.1 to 25 mass% of 4H-SiC silicon carbide crystals and 50 to 99.9 mass% of 6H-SiC silicon carbide crystals in the silicon carbide crystals.
A method for producing a silicon carbide ceramic according to any one of Claims 1 to 4, wherein a content amount of a nitrogen in the silicon carbide ceramic to be produced is 0.01 mass% or less.

A method for producing a silicon carbide ceramic according to any one of Claims 1 to 5, wherein: metal silicon powders are contained in the forming raw material; and the silicon carbide ceramic to be produced contains a plurality of silicon carbide particles and silicon for binding the silicon carbide particles to each other.
A method for producing a silicon carbide ceramic according to Claim 6, wherein an average particle diameter of the silicon carbide particles is 10 to 50 pm.
A method for producing a silicon carbide ceramic according to any one of Claims 1 to 7, wherein a porosity of the silicon carbide ceramic to be produced is 30 to 65%.

A method for producing a honeycomb structure which prepares a honeycomb structure being a honeycomb structural silicon carbide ceramic by a method for producing a silicon carbide ceramic according to any one of Claims 1 to 8.
